body:
I think instead of adding another dynamically computed msgid, in this case one could just as easily store the results of the `ExecuteTemplate` calls in variables and put the `ctx.Locale.Tr` invocation in the `if` (and move the `if` down here).

In turn, I would get rid of the `$is{Old,New}CommitValid` variables, given they're only used once.

(in fact, these `ExecuteTemplate` calls look repetitive enough that one might want a separate template for them, that includes the `$.Repo.IsCommitValid` invocation, etc.)

Thanks for the review comments.

@fogti wrote in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/15271#issuecomment-27839608:

> I think instead of adding another dynamically computed msgid, in this case one could just as easily store the results of the `ExecuteTemplate` calls in variables and put the `ctx.Locale.Tr` invocation in the `if` (and move the `if` down here).

Sure, that's a good approach as it eliminates the need for the change in `allowed-masked-usage.txt`.  Implemented in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/compare/d80b3bd4cc4b3bf26fddae0b1f5a05dcaeff95b9..c7b8be96172cb99438385fa4b392de44f07e0da0 

> In turn, I would get rid of the `$is{Old,New}CommitValid` variables, given they're only used once.

At some point in the draft these were reused in the buttons; I've restored that reuse in https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/compare/d80b3bd4cc4b3bf26fddae0b1f5a05dcaeff95b9..c7b8be96172cb99438385fa4b392de44f07e0da0
